{{Short description|Genus of extinct fish}} {{Speciesbox | fossil_range = Early [[Eocene]]
(late [[Ypresian]]), ~{{fossilrange|50.4|49.11}}{{Period fossil range|Paleogene|50.4|49.11}} | image = Exeomastix zabimaru (holotype, IGVR 64081–64082).png | image_caption = Holotype under natural light (A, B) and coated in alcohol for improved visualization (C, D) | display_parents = 2 | genus = Exeomastix | parent_authority =Calzoni, Giusberti & Carnevale, [[2026 in paleoichthyology|2026]] | species = zabimaru | authority = (Calzoni, Giusberti & Carnevale
''in'' Calzoni et al., 2026) | synonyms = * ''Eomastix'' {{small|Calzoni, Giusberti & Carnevale ''in'' Calzoni et al., 2026 (''non'' Jaschhof, 2009; [[preoccupied]])}} }} '''''Exeomastix''''' ({{lit|former dawn whip}}) is an [[extinct]] genus of [[cutlassfish]] (family Trichiuridae) known from the early [[Eocene]] ([[Ypresian]] age) [[Chiusole Formation]] of Italy. The genus contains a [[Monotypic taxon|single species]], '''''Exeomastix zabimaru''''', known from a skeleton preserved on a [[Compression fossil|slab and counterslab]]. It is characterized by its thin, ribbon-like body form, a fang at the front of the upper jaw, and a reduced, forked [[caudal fin]]. ''Exeomastix'' is the oldest trichiurid in the fossil record known from articulated remains. == Discovery and naming == [[File:Italian marine lagerstätten (Bolca, Monte Solane, and Solteri).png|thumb|left|[[Type locality (biology)|Type locality]] (Monte Solane) in Verona, Italy]] The ''Exeomastix'' fossil material was discovered at the Monte Solane locality, representing [[lagerstätte]] outcrops of the [[Chiusole Formation]] near the village of [[Sant'Ambrogio di Valpolicella]] in [[Province of Verona|Verona]], Italy. The specimen is [[Accession number (cultural property)|accessioned]] as part of the General Inventory of the Verona Province (IGVR; including the ''Museo di Storia Naturale di Verona'' and ''Antiquarium of San Giorgio di Valpolicella''). It consists of a nearly complete skeleton including the skull, preserved as a [[Compression fossil|part and counterpart]], catalogued together as IGVR 64081 and IGVR 64082. An initial report on the Monte Solane fish fossil assemblage in 2014 figured IGVR 64082, identifying it as [[Trichiuridae]] gen. indet. [[cf.]] ''[[Anenchelum]]'' (an indeterminate trichiurid genus comparable to ''Anenchelum''). In March 2026, Pietro Calzoni and colleagues [[Species description|described]] ''Eomastix zabimaru'' as a new genus and species of early cutlassfish based on these fossil remains, designating IGVR 64081–64082 as the [[holotype]] specimen. This initially proposed [[Genus|generic name]], ''Eomastix'', combines the [[Greek language|Greek]] words {{lang|grc|[[:wikt:ἠώς|ἠώς]]}} ({{lang|grc|ēṓs}}), meaning {{gloss|dawn}}, and {{lang|grc|[[:wikt:μάστιξ|μάστιξ]]}} ({{lang|grc|mắstīx}}), meaning {{gloss|whip}}. The former root alludes to both the ancient status of this taxon in relation to other trichiurids (at the {{gloss|dawn}} of the evolution of the clade), as well as its discovery in rocks dated to the [[Eocene]], while the latter root alludes to its thin, slender form. This genus name was [[Homonym (biology)|preoccupied]] by an [[Eomastix|insect of the same name]], so a replacement name had to be implemented. In July 2026, Calzoni et al. proposed the name ''Exeomastix'' to replace the unintentional initial homonym. The added [[Latin]] prefix {{lang|la|ex-}}, meaning {{gloss|former}}, alludes to the necessary replacement of the initially proposed (and preoccupied) name, ''Eomastix''. The [[Specific name (zoology)|specific name]], ''zabimaru'', is a [[Japanese language|Japanese]] word meaning {{gloss|snake tail}}, referencing the very thin caudal (tail) region of the species. ''Exeomastix'' is the earliest trichiurid known from articulated skeletal remains in the fossil record. The earliest putative trichiurid fossils are isolated teeth from the [[Paleocene]] ([[Paleogene]] epoch preceding the Eocene). Meanwhile, the next oldest articulated trichiurid is from the [[Lutetian]] (Eocene age following the Ypresian). == Description == [[File:Exeomastix zabimaru (skull reconstruction).png|thumb|left|Reconstructed skull of ''Exeomastix'']] ''Exeomastix'' is a small member of the family Trichiuridae (cutlassfish) with a long, compressed, ribbon-like body. The ''E. zabimaru'' holotype has a [[Fish measurement|standard length]] (SL) of {{convert|41.1|mm|in}}. None of the squamation (scale covering) is preserved in this specimen. The mouth is large, and the lower jaw projects past the upper jaw. The upper jaw has small teeth with a large fang in the [[premaxilla]] toward the front, while the lower jaw only has small conical teeth. It has 37 vertebrae in the vertebral column. The [[dorsal fin]]s are continuous, running along the length of the body, comprising a spiny dorsal fin with 15 rays toward the front, separated by a small notch from the soft dorsal fin at the rear, which has at least 15 rays. The [[anal fin]], which has at least 14 rays, is positioned approximately opposite the soft dorsal fin. ''Exeomastix'' has a forked, albeit notably reduced, [[caudal fin]], which contrasts with the filamentous condition of this fin in many [[Neontology|extant]] trichiurids, including ''[[Demissolinea]]'', ''[[Eupleurogrammus]]'', ''[[Lepturacanthus]]'', ''[[Tentoriceps]]'', and ''[[Trichiurus]]''. The pelvic girdle and [[Pelvic fin|associated fin]] are developed, contrasting with some extant trichiurids, in which it is absent (''Lepturacanthus'' and ''Trichiurus'') or reduced to a small spine (''[[Aphanopus]]'', ''[[Evoxymetopon]]'', and ''[[Lepidopus]]''). == References == {{Reflist|refs= {{Cite journal |last1=Calzoni |first1=Pietro |last2=Giusberti |first2=Luca |last3=Fornaciari
